trial_court: Family Court, Jagadhri, District Yamuna Nagar
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner's minor daughter is residing with her and has filed a complaint against the respondent-husband. The respondent-husband has filed a petition under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act at Jagadhri to harass the petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: While deciding the transfer application, courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of female litigants.
legal_principles.held: The Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants and transfer of legal proceedings from one Court to another should ordinarily be allowed, taking into consideration their convenience and the Courts should desist from putting female litigants under undue hardships.
cited_cases: Rajani Kishor Pardeshi Vs. Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) (12) SCC 237

legal_principles.principle: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under Section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both parties, their social strata, behavioural pattern, standard of life prior to and subsequent to marriage, and circumstances of both parties in eking out their livelihood.
legal_principles.held: The Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern, their standard of life prior to the marriage and subsequent thereto and the circumstances of both the parties in eking out their livelihood and under whose protective umbrella they are seeking their sustenance to life.
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs. A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the transfer application and directed that the petition be transferred to the competent Court of jurisdiction at Pehowa, District Kurukshetra.
